questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: During the basic control skills test, a driver may be asked to perform straight-line backing. According to the CDL manual, what does this exercise require?

answers.text: Back the vehicle in a straight line between two rows of cones without touching or knocking them over
Back the vehicle at highway speed while keeping the mirrors clear
Back the vehicle into a perpendicular loading dock from 200 feet away
Back the vehicle using only the center mirror without looking out the side windows

explanations.a: The CDL manual describes straight-line backing as backing the vehicle in a straight line between two rows of cones without touching or knocking them over or crossing the boundary lines.
explanations.b: Straight-line backing is done at slow, controlled speed, not highway speed.
explanations.c: Perpendicular dock backing is the alley dock exercise, not straight-line backing.
explanations.d: The exercise uses both side mirrors for reference; it is not a center-mirror-only exercise.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: The CDL manual sets different limits on how many times a driver may exit the vehicle for outside observations (looks) depending on the exercise. For straight-line backing specifically, what is the maximum allowed look count?

answers.text: Up to three looks are permitted for straight-line backing
Only one look is allowed for straight-line backing
Looks are unlimited as long as each look takes less than 30 seconds
No looks are permitted under any circumstances

explanations.a: Three looks exceed the limit for straight-line backing.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the maximum number of looks is two for most exercises, except for the straight-line backing exercise, which allows only one look.
explanations.c: There is no time-based exception; the limit is a count limit, not a duration limit.
explanations.d: One look is permitted; the limit is not zero.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: During any basic control skills exercise, the examiner tracks encroachments. According to the CDL manual, what is an encroachment and how is it scored?

answers.text: An encroachment is a gear-change made during a backing maneuver; each one adds 10 seconds
An encroachment is when the driver exceeds the speed limit; it results in immediate failure
An encroachment is any time any portion of the vehicle touches or crosses over an exercise boundary line or cone; each one counts as an error
An encroachment occurs only if all four wheels leave the lane simultaneously

explanations.a: Encroachments are boundary violations, not gear-change events.
explanations.b: The skills test is conducted at very low speeds; speed limits are not the scoring category.
explanations.c: The CDL manual defines an encroachment as any time any portion of the vehicle touches or crosses over an exercise boundary line or cone; each encroachment counts as an error.
explanations.d: Any portion of the vehicle touching a boundary is an encroachment, not only all-four-wheel departures.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: When a driver is permitted to exit the vehicle during a skills test exercise for an outside observation (look), the CDL manual prescribes a specific safety procedure for exiting. Which procedure matches the manual?

answers.text: Leave the engine running and the door open, then lean out to look
Ask the examiner to hold the steering wheel while the driver exits
Step off the running board with arms free to swing for balance
Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake; face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times when exiting

explanations.a: Leaving the engine running with the door open and leaning out does not place the vehicle in a secured state.
explanations.b: Having the examiner hold the wheel is not part of the procedure described in the manual.
explanations.c: Stepping off with arms free is the opposite of the manual's three-points-of-contact requirement.
explanations.d: The CDL manual requires the driver to place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake, then face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times when exiting to take an outside observation.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: During a skills test exercise, a driver stops forward motion and pulls the vehicle forward to correct position before resuming the backing maneuver. The CDL manual calls this a pull-up. How does the manual score pull-ups?

answers.text: Initial pull-ups are not penalized, but an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors
Every single pull-up counts as an automatic failure
Pull-ups are completely unlimited with no scoring consequence
Pull-ups count the same as encroachments, one error each

explanations.a: The CDL manual states drivers will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
explanations.b: Single pull-ups are not automatic failures; only excessive pull-ups accumulate errors.
explanations.c: Pull-ups are not completely unlimited; excessive use is penalized.
explanations.d: Pull-ups and encroachments are separate scoring categories with different rules.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: The CDL manual describes the offset back/right exercise for the basic control skills test. Which description matches the manual?

answers.text: The driver reverses straight backward over a distance equal to the trailer length

The driver is asked to back into a space to the right rear of the vehicle; the driver drives straight forward to the outer boundary and then backs the vehicle into the opposite lane until the front of the vehicle passes the first set of cones
The driver backs the vehicle onto a turntable and rotates 90 degrees to the right
The driver is asked to parallel park on the right side of the road in conventional fashion

explanations.a: The offset back/right is not a simple straight-line back to the rear.
explanations.b: The CDL manual describes the offset back/right as driving straight forward to the outer boundary and then backing the vehicle into the space to the right rear until the front of the vehicle passes the first set of cones without striking boundary lines or cones.
explanations.c: There is no turntable rotation exercise in the basic skills test.
explanations.d: Parallel parking on the right is a separate exercise called parallel park conventional.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: The CDL manual also describes an offset back/left exercise. How does offset back/left differ from offset back/right?

answers.text: Offset back/left is performed at twice the speed of offset back/right
Offset back/left uses a longer approach lane than offset back/right
In offset back/left the driver backs into a space to the left rear of the vehicle instead of the right rear
Offset back/left is not a scored exercise; it is only a demonstration

explanations.a: Both exercises are performed at slow, controlled backing speed; speed is not the difference.
explanations.b: Approach-lane length is not the distinguishing factor between the two exercises.
explanations.c: The CDL manual describes offset back/left as backing into a space to the left rear of the vehicle, compared with offset back/right which targets the right rear.
explanations.d: Offset back/left is a fully scored exercise, not a demonstration.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.keyword: drive forward to outer boundary first
questions.text: Both the offset back/right and offset back/left exercises begin with the same setup. According to the CDL manual, what is that setup move?

answers.text: The driver first backs the vehicle to the rear boundary of the exercise area
The driver begins by turning 45 degrees toward the target space
The driver must first parallel park and then reposition to begin the offset
The driver drives straight forward to the outer boundary before beginning the rearward backing maneuver

explanations.a: The exercise begins with a forward drive, not a rearward move to the rear boundary.
explanations.b: A 45-degree turn is not the described setup move.
explanations.c: Parallel parking is a separate exercise; it is not a required setup for the offset exercises.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to drive straight forward to the outer boundary and from that position begin backing the vehicle into the target space.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: For the offset back/right and offset back/left exercises, the CDL manual specifies the maximum number of outside observations (looks) a driver is permitted. What is that limit?

answers.text: A maximum of two looks for these exercises
A maximum of four looks for offset exercises
Looks are not permitted for offset exercises; the driver must use mirrors only
A maximum of three looks, but only if an encroachment occurs

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the maximum number of looks is two for most basic control skills exercises, which includes the offset backing exercises.
explanations.b: Four looks exceeds the manual's maximum.
explanations.c: Looks are permitted for offset exercises within the stated limit.
explanations.d: Three looks exceeds the manual's two-look maximum, and the right to look is not contingent on an encroachment.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.keyword: parallel park driver side left space
questions.text: The CDL manual describes two parallel parking exercises. In the parallel park driver side exercise, on which side of the vehicle is the parking space located?

answers.text: To the right of the vehicle, along the right curb
To the left of the vehicle; the driver backs into a space on the driver's side
Behind the vehicle, requiring a straight-line back into the spot
The space can be on either side; the examiner chooses at random

explanations.a: Driver-side parking is on the left; conventional parallel parking is on the right.
explanations.b: The CDL manual describes parallel park driver side as a space to the left; the driver drives past the entrance to the space and backs in from the driver's side.
explanations.c: The exercise uses backing, but the space is lateral (to the side), not directly behind the vehicle.
explanations.d: Each exercise is defined by a specific side; they are not interchangeable.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: In contrast to driver-side parallel parking, the CDL manual describes parallel park conventional. Which feature distinguishes conventional from driver-side parallel parking?

answers.text: In conventional parallel parking, the vehicle backs in from the left side into a right-side space after driving past
In conventional parallel parking, the vehicle drives forward into the space without backing
In conventional parallel parking, the parking space is on the right side of the vehicle; the driver drives past the space and backs in
Conventional parallel parking is not a scored exercise; only driver-side is scored

explanations.a: Conventional parallel parking backs into a right-side space, not a left-side space.
explanations.b: Parallel parking requires backing; there is no forward-only parallel parking exercise in the manual.
explanations.c: The CDL manual describes parallel park conventional as parking in a space to the right of the vehicle; the driver drives past the entrance and backs in.
explanations.d: Both driver-side and conventional parallel parking are scored skills test exercises.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: For both parallel parking exercises, the CDL manual states a specific requirement about where the vehicle must end up at the conclusion of the maneuver. Which requirement matches the manual?

answers.text: At least the rear half of the vehicle must be inside the space
The front bumper may extend up to five feet beyond the front boundary
Only the trailer must be within the cones; the tractor may extend outside
The entire vehicle must be completely inside the space defined by the boundary cones

explanations.a: Requiring only the rear half is weaker than the manual's standard; the entire vehicle must be inside.
explanations.b: The manual requires the vehicle to be within the boundaries, not extending five feet beyond.
explanations.c: The manual requires the entire vehicle, not just the trailer, to be inside the space.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states the driver is required to get the entire vehicle completely into the space defined by the boundary cones.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: The CDL manual describes the approach for both parallel parking exercises. What approach position does the driver use before beginning to back?

answers.text: Drive past the entrance to the parking space with the vehicle parallel to the parking area, then back in
Back up from 100 feet in front of the space and enter in a single continuous reverse maneuver
Stop with the front of the vehicle at the entrance to the space and then nose in forward
Approach at a 45-degree angle to the space and pivot into position

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to drive past the entrance to the parallel parking space with the vehicle parallel to the parking area, and then back into the space.
explanations.b: Beginning from 100 feet in front is not the described approach; the driver drives past first.
explanations.c: Nosing in forward is not how parallel parking is done in the manual's description.
explanations.d: A 45-degree approach is not the described setup position.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.keyword: no crossing front side rear boundaries
questions.text: Both parallel parking exercises require the vehicle to stay within boundaries. According to the CDL manual, which boundaries must the vehicle not cross?

answers.text: Only the rear boundary; the front and sides may be crossed briefly
The front, side, and rear boundaries marked by cones must not be crossed
Only the side boundaries matter; the front and rear are not scored
No boundaries are scored during parallel parking; only the look count matters

explanations.a: The manual requires all three boundaries — front, side, and rear — to be respected.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the driver must back into the space without crossing the front, side, or rear boundaries marked by cones.
explanations.c: All three boundaries are scored; none are exempt.
explanations.d: Boundary crossings (encroachments) are always scored; looks are a separate category.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: The alley dock is a specific backing exercise described in the CDL manual. According to the manual, which backing technique is prescribed for the alley dock?

answers.text: Blind-side backing from the passenger side of the vehicle
Straight-line backing in the same lane without any turn
Sight-side backing, where the driver positions the vehicle to back into the alley with the driver's side toward the alley opening
Backing guided only by the convex spot mirror at slow walking speed

explanations.a: The manual prescribes sight-side (driver's side) backing, not blind-side backing.
explanations.b: The alley dock involves an angled back into an alley, not a straight-line maneuver.
explanations.c: The CDL manual specifies the alley dock is a sight-side back into the alley, meaning the driver positions to back with the driver's side toward the alley opening for maximum visibility.
explanations.d: Both mirrors are used; there is no convex-mirror-only restriction.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.keyword: rear within three feet of alley back
questions.text: The CDL manual sets a specific stopping-distance target for the rear of the vehicle in the alley dock exercise. How close to the rear of the alley must the rear of the vehicle come?

answers.text: Within 10 feet of the rear of the alley
Within 6 feet of the rear of the alley
Touching the rear cone is required
Within 3 feet of the rear of the alley without touching the boundary lines or cones

explanations.a: 10 feet is farther than the manual's target distance.
explanations.b: 6 feet exceeds the manual's published maximum gap.
explanations.c: Touching the rear cone is an encroachment and counts as an error.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states the driver must bring the rear of the vehicle within 3 feet of the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.keyword: vehicle must be straight in alley
questions.text: After completing the alley dock, the CDL manual states a specific orientation requirement for the vehicle inside the alley. Which requirement matches the manual?

answers.text: The vehicle must be straight within the alley/lane when the maneuver is completed
The vehicle may be at an angle as long as all wheels are inside the boundaries
The front of the vehicle must point toward the exit of the alley
The vehicle can be at any angle as long as the rear is within 3 feet of the back wall

explanations.a: The CDL manual specifically states the vehicle must be straight within the alley/lane when the maneuver is completed.
explanations.b: An angled vehicle is not acceptable; the manual requires the vehicle to be straight.
explanations.c: The front pointing toward the exit would mean the vehicle is pointed the wrong direction since the vehicle backed in.
explanations.d: The final position requirement includes both the 3-foot depth standard and the straight-vehicle standard.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: Before beginning to back in the alley dock exercise, the CDL manual specifies the setup position. Which setup matches the manual?

answers.text: Position the vehicle perpendicular to the alley entrance, then back in at a right angle
Drive past the alley and position the vehicle parallel to the outer boundary, then back into the alley
Stop directly in front of the alley entrance and back straight in
Position the vehicle at a 60-degree angle to the alley, then back at that angle

explanations.a: Positioning perpendicular to the entrance is not the manual's setup.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to drive past the alley and position the vehicle parallel to the outer boundary, then back into the alley from that position.
explanations.c: Stopping directly in front and backing straight in would make this a straight-line exercise, not an alley dock.
explanations.d: A 60-degree setup angle is not described in the manual.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.keyword: lane change test left then right
questions.text: During the on-road driving test, the CDL manual describes the lane change sequence an examiner may require. Which sequence matches the manual?

answers.text: The driver is asked to change lanes to the right first and then to the left
The driver changes lanes randomly based on traffic flow
The driver is asked to change lanes to the left, and then back to the right
The driver must change lanes three times continuously without stopping

explanations.a: The manual specifies left first, then right — not right first.
explanations.b: The examiner directs the lane changes; they are not random.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states that during multiple-lane portions of the test, the driver will be asked to change lanes to the left and then back to the right.
explanations.d: The manual describes a two-lane-change sequence, not three continuous changes.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.keyword: left turn finish right of center
questions.text: The CDL manual's lane usage rules specify where the vehicle should end up after completing a left turn on a multiple-lane road. Which instruction matches the manual?

answers.text: After a left turn, the vehicle should end up in the left-most lane to be ready for the next turn
After a left turn, the vehicle should cross all lanes to reach the right-most lane immediately
After a left turn, the vehicle should stop in the intersection briefly to check for cross-traffic
After a left turn, the vehicle should finish the turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line

explanations.a: Staying in the left-most lane after a left turn is not the manual's rule.
explanations.b: Immediately crossing all lanes is unsafe and is not the manual's instruction.
explanations.c: Stopping in the intersection after completing a turn is unsafe and not what the manual prescribes.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states a left turn should finish in the lane directly to the right of the center line on a multiple-lane road.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.keyword: right turn finish right-most curb lane
questions.text: After completing a right turn, the CDL manual specifies which lane the vehicle should finish in. Which instruction matches the manual?

answers.text: Finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane
Finish a right turn in the center lane
Finish a right turn in the left-most lane
Right turns may be completed in any available lane

explanations.a: The CDL manual states drivers should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
explanations.b: Finishing in the center lane after a right turn is not the manual's instruction.
explanations.c: Finishing in the left-most lane after a right turn is unsafe and opposite the manual's rule.
explanations.d: There is a specific lane requirement; any available lane is not correct.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.text: While driving through an intersection, the CDL manual gives a specific lane-discipline rule. Which rule matches the manual?

answers.text: Lane changes may be made in the intersection if the new lane is to the right
Do not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
Lane changes in the intersection are allowed when the examiner directs them
Multiple lane changes are permitted in intersections during an emergency stop only

explanations.a: The manual prohibits lane changes in intersections regardless of direction.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states drivers must not change lanes while proceeding through an intersection.
explanations.c: Examiner direction does not override the no-lane-change-in-intersection rule.
explanations.d: There is no emergency-stop exception to the lane-change rule in the manual.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.objective: 7.6 Turns (right, left, U-turn, with and without curb)
questions.text: During approach to a turn, the CDL manual warns against unsafe coasting. How does the manual define unsafe coasting?

answers.text: Coasting is always unsafe and is never permitted in any gear
Unsafe coasting means traveling at any speed under 10 mph in gear
Unsafe coasting occurs when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
Unsafe coasting means running the engine below idle speed on a downgrade

explanations.a: Some brief out-of-gear operation is normal during smooth gear changes; the manual defines a specific threshold.
explanations.b: Vehicle speed is not the manual's definition of unsafe coasting.
explanations.c: The CDL manual defines unsafe coasting as when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle.
explanations.d: Engine speed below idle is not the manual's definition of unsafe coasting.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.objective: 7.6 Turns (right, left, U-turn, with and without curb)
questions.keyword: do not shift in turns intersections
questions.text: The CDL manual lists specific locations where shifting gears is prohibited during normal driving. Which rule matches the manual?

answers.text: Do not shift gears on straight sections of road
Do not shift gears when the speedometer is above 30 mph
Do not shift gears when any passenger is standing
Do not shift gears in turns and intersections

explanations.a: Gear shifting on straight road sections is normal; the prohibition is in turns and intersections.
explanations.b: A 30-mph threshold is not the manual's shifting prohibition.
explanations.c: Passenger standing is a bus safety rule unrelated to the gear-shifting prohibition.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states drivers must not shift gears in turns and intersections.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.objective: 7.6 Turns (right, left, U-turn, with and without curb)
questions.text: After completing a turn during the on-road driving test, the CDL manual specifies an immediate follow-up action regarding the turn signal. Which action matches the manual?

answers.text: Make sure the turn signal is off after the turn is completed
Leave the turn signal flashing to warn drivers behind you
Sound the horn once to signal other drivers that the turn is complete
Turn the steering wheel back hard to center the signal stalk

explanations.a: The CDL manual states drivers must make sure the turn signal is off after the turn is completed.
explanations.b: Leaving the signal flashing confuses other drivers about the vehicle's next intended move.
explanations.c: Horn use is not the signal-cancel action described in the manual.
explanations.d: The signal stalk does not require a hard wheel input to cancel; canceling is a specific manual step.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.objective: 7.6 Turns (right, left, U-turn, with and without curb)
questions.keyword: stop behind stop line for turn
questions.text: If a driver must stop before making a turn (due to a stop sign, signal, or cross-traffic), the CDL manual gives specific instructions about where to stop. Which instruction matches the manual?

answers.text: Stop with the front of the vehicle over the stop line so the examiner can see it clearly
Come to a smooth stop without skidding, and come to a complete stop behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign
Stop in the intersection itself so cross-traffic can see the vehicle clearly
The vehicle may stop anywhere as long as it is parallel to the curb

explanations.a: The front of the vehicle must be behind the stop line, not over it.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to come to a smooth stop without skidding and come to a complete stop behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign.
explanations.c: Stopping in the intersection blocks cross-traffic and is prohibited.
explanations.d: Parallel to the curb describes parking position; the turn-approach stop must be behind the control line.

questions.name: Basic Vehicle Control and Maneuvering
questions.objective: 7.6 Turns (right, left, U-turn, with and without curb)
questions.keyword: both hands on wheel unless shifting
questions.text: The CDL manual's general steering guidance for the on-road driving test includes a specific rule about hand position. Which rule matches the manual?

answers.text: Keep one hand on the wheel and one on the gear shift at all times for readiness
The driver may use a single finger on the wheel during straight-line driving
Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting gears; once the shift is complete, return both hands to the wheel immediately
Hands may be taken off the wheel whenever the vehicle is traveling below 10 mph

explanations.a: One hand on the gear shift at all times is inconsistent with the manual's two-hands standard.
explanations.b: Single-finger steering is unsafe and is not the manual's guidance.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states drivers must keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, and once the shift is complete, must return both hands to the wheel immediately.
explanations.d: Speed is not the manual's criterion for releasing hands from the wheel.
